Privacy Policy

Effective date: 12 November 2026

This policy covers the free DevlogMaker desktop application (the "App") and this website, https://glumbis.github.io/devlogmaker-app.

1. The short version

  • We don't collect anything. There are no DevlogMaker accounts, servers, telemetry, crash reports, analytics or cookies. We never receive your code, clips, scripts, videos or keys.
  • Your project stays on your computer. The App works on your files locally.
  • AI requests go straight from your computer to the services you choose (Anthropic or Claude Desktop, ElevenLabs, optionally Google Gemini), under your own accounts with them.
  • Publishing happens only when you confirm it, directly from your computer to the platforms you pick.

2. What the App stores on your computer

Only on your device; we have no access to it:

  • Your projects: the game folders you add, the settings file (devlog.toml) and the run folders (.devlog/) inside each game folder, including scripts, shot lists, captured footage, narration audio, music, rendered videos and publish drafts.
  • App settings and the game list: in %APPDATA%\DevlogMaker (Windows) or ~/Library/Application Support/DevlogMaker (macOS).
  • Secrets: your API keys and publishing credentials (such as a Discord webhook, Bluesky app password or Mastodon token) are kept in your operating system's keychain (Windows Credential Manager or macOS Keychain). If you set up YouTube publishing, the Google sign-in token is stored in your project at .devlog/youtube_token.json.

Web-page capture opens your page in a browser on your computer; nothing is uploaded.

3. What is sent to AI services, and when

To make a devlog, the App sends the following, directly from your computer:

Step Sent to What is sent
Game profile (when first built or refreshed) Anthropic (Claude) Your game's name, engine and pitch; the text of project documents (README, docs/, design docs); a list of file paths in the project; the subjects of recent commits
Change summary Anthropic (Claude) The game profile; commit hashes, subjects and messages; filtered code changes (diffs) of source files, with generated, vendored, ignored and binary files removed; names of changed assets; your own notes, if you add any
Script and shot list Anthropic (Claude) The game profile, the topic summary, your chosen length, tone, audience and format, and the names of media files available for shots
Publish text (title, description, tags, post) Anthropic (Claude) Game name and pitch, video title and length, and the topic summary
Narration ElevenLabs The narration text of each segment, your chosen voice and voice settings; the App also fetches the list of available voices
Background music (only if you turn it on) Google (Gemini API) A music prompt built from your game's name, pitch and the devlog's tone, or your own prompt

With your Anthropic API key, the Claude steps go to Anthropic's API. With Claude Desktop, the App hands those steps to Claude Desktop on your computer instead, and Claude Desktop sends them to Anthropic under your Claude account, together with your chat.

Not sent to any AI service: your gameplay clips, screenshots, images, rendered videos, keys, or files you exclude with ignore rules. Commit author names and email addresses are not included. Code that appears on code cards in your video comes from your repository; review it before publishing if your code is private.

These providers process the data under their own terms and privacy policies, which say how long they keep it and whether they use it to improve their services: Anthropic, ElevenLabs, Google.

4. Publishing

When you publish, the App sends the video and its text directly from your computer to the platforms you chose (YouTube, Discord, Bluesky, Mastodon). Those platforms handle it under their own terms; we don't receive it.

5. YouTube API Services

The App's YouTube publishing feature uses YouTube API Services. If you use it:

  • What is accessed: you sign in with your Google account and grant the App permission to upload videos and manage your YouTube videos, thumbnails and captions (the scopes youtube.upload and youtube.force-ssl). The App uses this only to upload the video you confirmed, with its title, description, tags, privacy status, thumbnail and captions, and to read back the new video's ID to build its link.
  • Where it is stored: the Google sign-in token is stored only on your computer, in your project at .devlog/youtube_token.json. The video ID and link are saved in your project's run folder. None of this is sent to us.
  • Sharing: we don't receive or share your YouTube data. The App sends it only to Google.
  • Deleting and revoking: delete .devlog/youtube_token.json to remove the token from your computer, and revoke the App's access at any time on the Google security settings page.

By using YouTube publishing, you agree to the YouTube Terms of Service. Google's processing of your data is described in the Google Privacy Policy.

6. This website and the downloads

The website is static and hosted on GitHub Pages; the installers are downloaded from GitHub Releases. The site sets no cookies and uses no analytics, tracking or third-party scripts, so there is no cookie banner. GitHub, as the host, processes technical data such as your IP address to deliver the pages and files and to keep them secure; see the GitHub General Privacy Statement. If you open an issue to contact us, GitHub shows it publicly under your GitHub account.

7. Children

The App is not directed at children under 13 (or the minimum age in your country). Some services it connects to, such as Google's Gemini API, require users to be 18 or older.

8. Changes

If this policy changes, the new version is posted here with a new effective date. If DevlogMaker ever adds accounts or a paid service, this policy will be updated before that launches.

9. Contact

Questions or requests: open an issue at github.com/glumbis/devlogmaker-app/issues.
